findings.body: Raise: Not done. A fix created by the normal default Narrow path can reach a review stop, but its question names it as “Review finding left open by …” and describes its delivery as “A review no longer finds …”. Those phrases come from the generated fix state at src/forge/close.py:405-407; this line passes them through after stripping paths. The owner still cannot tell in plain words what the fix is or what it delivers.
findings.title: Not done: follow-up fixes describe a review record instead of the item

findings.body: Raise: Functional. At land's own three-fix-round review stop, this line prints the question and line 86 re-raises the original blocked-review refusal. That refusal's Next line is `forge work`, while the newly recorded stop requires `forge close --resolve` before the review can continue. The command therefore ends with an instruction that contradicts the decision it just requested.
findings.title: Stopped land directs the coordinator back to work instead of the owner's choice

findings.body: Raise: Gate. The named later-round spec proof checks the intro, Next line and one blocker line, but never checks the item's delivery or any of the three choices; it would pass with those parts of the question removed. The named land proofs in tests/test_land.py likewise check only the question's opening lines and that `forge next` repeats them, so they can pass when both commands omit the choices. These entries do not prove the complete ready-to-ask questions they claim.
